input.name: images
notes: Square input only. Export rejects a non-square imgsz, and height and width are 640 by default.
Batch size 1 only. The graph declares a dynamic batch axis, but batches of 2 or more fail in 1.7.0.
Divide by 255 after the resize. There is no mean or std normalization.

outputs.name: pred_logits
outputs.meaning: One logit per query and class. Sigmoid is not applied. queries is 300 for every size.

outputs.name: pred_boxes
outputs.meaning: cx, cy, w, h of each query, normalized 0 to 1 of the input. The input is the whole image stretched, so these are also fractions of the original image.

postprocess: Flatten the [queries, nc] scores and take the top 300 (max_det, 300 by default). For flat index k, the query is k // nc and the class is k % nc. One query can yield several classes.
Keep the pairs whose score is above the confidence threshold (0.25 by default).
Convert the query's box to x1 = cx - w / 2, y1 = cy - h / 2, x2 = cx + w / 2, y2 = cy + h / 2. Multiply x by the original image width and y by the original image height.
There is no NMS and the iou threshold is not used. D-FINE predicts a set of boxes, and export with nms=True raises NotImplementedError.
LibreYOLO does not clip these boxes, so an edge can sit slightly outside the image.

outputs.name: pred_logits
outputs.meaning: One logit per query and class. Sigmoid is not applied. queries is 300 for every size.

outputs.name: pred_boxes
outputs.meaning: cx, cy, w, h of each query, normalized 0 to 1 of the input. The input is the whole image stretched, so these are also fractions of the original image.

outputs.name: pred_masks
outputs.meaning: One mask per query, sigmoid already applied. mask_h is height / 4 and mask_w is width / 4, 160 x 160 at 640 x 640.

postprocess: Flatten the [queries, nc] scores and take the top 300 (max_det, 300 by default). For flat index k, the query is k // nc and the class is k % nc. One query can yield several classes.
Keep the pairs whose score is above the confidence threshold (0.25 by default).
Convert the query's box to x1 = cx - w / 2, y1 = cy - h / 2, x2 = cx + w / 2, y2 = cy + h / 2. Multiply x by the original image width and y by the original image height.

For each kept pair, take its query's mask. Resize it with bilinear interpolation and half-pixel centers (align_corners=False, no antialiasing) to height x width, then again to the original image size.
A pixel belongs to the mask when its value is 0.5 or more.
Clear every mask pixel outside the box. Pixel (x, y) stays only when x1 <= x < x2 and y1 <= y < y2, in original-image pixels.
There is no NMS and the iou threshold is not used. D-FINE predicts a set of boxes, and export with nms=True raises NotImplementedError.
LibreYOLO does not clip the boxes of a .pt predict, so an edge can sit slightly outside the image. Its ONNX backend clips them to the image.
